statement: Octopuses have three hearts.
explanation: Two branchial hearts pump blood through the gills, while the third (systemic heart) pumps oxygenated blood to the rest of the body.

statement: Bats are completely blind.
explanation: All bat species can see. Most have perfectly functional eyesight, and some species of fruit bats have exceptional night vision.

statement: Wombat droppings are cube-shaped.
explanation: Wombats produce uniquely cube-shaped feces due to the elastic nature of their intestinal walls, which helps mark territory.

statement: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
explanation: The collective noun for a group of flamingos is indeed a 'flamboyance', reflecting their vivid pink plumage.

statement: Elephants are the only mammals that cannot jump.
explanation: While adult elephants cannot jump due to their massive body mass and skeletal structure, they are not the only mammals unable to do so; sloths, hippos, and rhinos also cannot jump.

statement: Bulls are enraged by the color red.
explanation: Cattle are red-green colorblind. Bulls in bullfighting react to the movement of the cape, not its color.

statement: A snail can sleep for up to three years.
explanation: Snails can enter a state of hibernation or estivation for up to three years to survive drought or cold conditions.

statement: Goldfish have a memory span of only three seconds.
explanation: Scientific studies have demonstrated goldfish can retain memories for months and can be trained to complete tasks.

statement: Koala fingerprints are nearly indistinguishable from human fingerprints.
explanation: Koalas independently evolved fingerprints that are so similar to human ones they can confuse forensic investigators.

statement: A shrimp's heart is located in its head.
explanation: Shrimp have an open circulatory system, and their heart is situated in the cephalothorax — the fused head and thorax region.

statement: Polar bears have white fur.
explanation: Polar bear fur is actually transparent and hollow. It appears white because it reflects visible light. Their skin underneath is black.

statement: Frogs absorb water through their skin.
explanation: Frogs do not drink water with their mouths. They absorb water directly through a permeable area on their belly called the 'drinking patch'.

statement: Tigers have striped skin under their striped fur.
explanation: The stripe pattern of a tiger is not only on its fur but is also pigmented into the skin, so a shaved tiger would still show stripes.

statement: Camels store water in their humps.
explanation: Camel humps store fat, not water. This fat can be metabolised for energy and produces water as a byproduct during digestion.

statement: Butterflies taste with their feet.
explanation: Butterflies have chemoreceptors on their tarsi (feet), allowing them to taste plants the moment they land on them.

statement: A crocodile cannot stick its tongue out.
explanation: A crocodile's tongue is attached along its entire length to the floor of its mouth, making it impossible to stick out.

statement: Owls can rotate their heads 360 degrees.
explanation: Owls can rotate their heads up to 270 degrees in either direction, but not a full 360 degrees.

statement: Ostriches bury their heads in the sand when frightened.
explanation: This is a popular myth. Ostriches dig holes in the ground for nests, and when tending to eggs may appear to have their heads down, but they do not hide from predators this way.

statement: The mantis shrimp has 16 types of color receptors.
explanation: While humans have 3 types of color-detecting cones, the mantis shrimp has 16, enabling it to see a vast spectrum including UV and infrared light.

statement: Penguins propose to their mates with a pebble.
explanation: Male Gentoo penguins search for the perfect pebble to present to a female. If she accepts it, they mate and use it to help build their nest.

statement: Dolphins sleep with one eye open.
explanation: Dolphins practice unihemispheric sleep — one half of their brain sleeps while the other remains conscious, allowing them to breathe and watch for threats.

statement: Sharks are the only fish that can blink.
explanation: Sharks are not the only fish that blink. Mudskippers can genuinely blink by lowering their eyes into dermal cups to keep them moist on land. Most sharks don't blink, though some have a protective nictitating membrane.

statement: Cows have four stomachs.
explanation: Cows have one stomach with four distinct compartments: the rumen, reticulum, omasum, and abomasum.

statement: Lemmings commit mass suicide by jumping off cliffs.
explanation: This myth was largely popularized by a 1958 Disney documentary that staged the event. Lemmings do not deliberately kill themselves.

statement: An octopus can edit its own genetic code.
explanation: Octopuses (and some other cephalopods) can recode their own RNA to alter protein function, allowing rapid adaptation to environmental changes like temperature.

statement: A group of crows is called a murder.
explanation: 'Murder' is the traditional collective noun for crows, likely inspired by folklore about their dark plumage and scavenging habits.

statement: Sea otters sometimes hold hands while sleeping.
explanation: Floating otters, especially mothers and pups, hold paws or wrap themselves in kelp so they don't drift apart while they rest.

statement: The blue whale is the largest animal known ever to have existed.
explanation: Blue whales can reach about 30 metres in length and weigh up to roughly 180 tonnes, larger than any known dinosaur.

statement: Hummingbirds can fly backwards.
explanation: Their unique shoulder joints let their wings rotate in a figure-eight, allowing them to hover and fly in reverse.

statement: Giraffes have the same number of neck bones as humans.
explanation: Both have seven cervical vertebrae; a giraffe's are just enormously elongated.

statement: Honey bees communicate the location of food with a 'waggle dance'.
explanation: The angle and duration of the dance tell other bees the direction and distance to a food source.

statement: Cats cannot taste sweetness.
explanation: Cats lack a functional gene for the sweet taste receptor, so sugar means nothing to their tongues.

statement: A newborn kangaroo is about the size of a jellybean.
explanation: A joey is only around 2 cm long at birth and crawls into its mother's pouch to continue developing.

statement: Axolotls can regrow lost limbs.
explanation: These salamanders can regenerate limbs, spinal cord tissue, and even parts of their heart and brain.

statement: Sloths can hold their breath for up to 40 minutes.
explanation: By slowing their heart rate, sloths can stay underwater far longer than dolphins can.

statement: Male seahorses give birth to the young.
explanation: Females deposit eggs into the male's brood pouch, where he fertilises and carries them until they hatch.

statement: Elephants can recognise themselves in a mirror.
explanation: Passing the mirror self-recognition test is rare in the animal kingdom; elephants, great apes and dolphins have done it.

statement: The snapping shrimp can create a sound louder than a gunshot underwater.
explanation: Its claw snaps shut so fast that it produces a collapsing bubble, generating a sound of around 200 decibels.

statement: Crows can recognise individual human faces.
explanation: Studies show crows remember faces that have threatened them and can even teach other crows to be wary of those people.

statement: A cheetah can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in about three seconds.
explanation: Cheetahs are the fastest land animals, reaching around 100 km/h in just a few strides.

statement: The platypus is a mammal that lays eggs.
explanation: Along with echidnas, the platypus is one of only a few egg-laying mammals, known as monotremes.

statement: Starfish do not have a brain.
explanation: Sea stars have a decentralised nervous system with a nerve ring and radial nerves instead of a central brain.

statement: No two dogs have the same nose print.
explanation: Just like human fingerprints, the ridge pattern on a dog's nose is unique to each animal.

statement: Male emperor penguins incubate the eggs on their feet.
explanation: Through the Antarctic winter, males balance a single egg on their feet under a warm brood pouch while the females feed at sea.

statement: A woodpecker's tongue wraps around the back of its skull.
explanation: The long tongue curls around the skull and acts like a cushion, helping to protect the brain during rapid pecking.

statement: Tardigrades can survive the vacuum of outer space.
explanation: In a 2007 experiment, tardigrades exposed to open space survived, and some even went on to reproduce.

statement: The Arctic tern makes the longest migration of any animal.
explanation: It flies from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back each year, covering roughly 70,000 km.

statement: Dolphins call each other using signature whistles.
explanation: Each dolphin develops a unique whistle that works much like a name, which other dolphins use to address it.

statement: Giant pandas spend up to 14 hours a day eating.
explanation: Bamboo is low in nutrients, so pandas must eat 12 to 38 kg of it daily to meet their energy needs.

statement: Sharks are older than trees.
explanation: Sharks have existed for around 450 million years, while the first trees appeared roughly 385 million years ago.

statement: Horses can sleep while standing up.
explanation: A special locking mechanism in their legs, the stay apparatus, lets horses doze on their feet without collapsing.

statement: Orcas are a species of dolphin.
explanation: Despite the name 'killer whale', the orca is the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family.

statement: Bats are the only mammals capable of true sustained flight.
explanation: Flying squirrels and sugar gliders only glide, while bats genuinely flap their wings to fly.

statement: A giraffe's tongue can be around 50 cm long.
explanation: The dark, prehensile tongue strips leaves from thorny acacia trees, and its dark colour is thought to protect against sunburn.

statement: Owls cannot move their eyeballs.
explanation: Their tube-shaped eyes are fixed in the skull, which is why owls need to turn their heads so far to look around.

statement: Spiders are not insects.
explanation: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs and two body segments, whereas insects have six legs and three body segments.

statement: A group of owls is called a parliament.
explanation: 'Parliament' is the traditional collective noun for owls, a nod to their wise reputation.

statement: Mosquitoes kill more humans than any other animal.
explanation: By spreading diseases such as malaria and dengue, mosquitoes are responsible for hundreds of thousands of deaths each year.

statement: An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain.
explanation: An ostrich eye is about 5 cm across, larger than its brain, and gives it excellent long-distance vision.

statement: Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of kilometres across several generations.
explanation: No single butterfly makes the whole round trip; it takes multiple generations to complete the journey between Canada and Mexico.

statement: Naked mole-rats do not feel pain from acid.
explanation: A mutation in their pain-sensing nerves means that acid, which usually burns, doesn't hurt them.

statement: Koalas can sleep up to 20 hours a day.
explanation: Their eucalyptus diet is low in energy and toxic, so koalas conserve energy by sleeping for most of the day.

statement: Octopuses have blue blood.
explanation: Their blood uses copper-based hemocyanin to carry oxygen, which turns blue when oxygenated, rather than iron-based haemoglobin.

statement: Pigs cannot sweat.
explanation: Pigs have very few functional sweat glands, so they wallow in mud to cool down and protect their skin from the sun.

statement: The giant panda is a true bear.
explanation: Genetic studies confirm giant pandas belong to the bear family, Ursidae, despite their unusual bamboo diet.

statement: A headless chicken named Mike lived for about 18 months in the 1940s.
explanation: The axe missed his brain stem and one ear, which was enough for Mike to survive and be fed with an eyedropper.

statement: Only female mosquitoes bite.
explanation: Females need the proteins in blood to develop their eggs, while males feed on nectar.

statement: Touching a baby bird will make its mother abandon it.
explanation: Most birds have a poor sense of smell and will not reject a chick that has been handled, though it is still best to leave wildlife alone.

statement: Daddy longlegs are the most venomous spiders but their fangs cannot bite humans.
explanation: This urban legend has never been supported; the venom of harvestmen and cellar spiders is not dangerous to people.

statement: Chameleons change colour mainly to blend in with their surroundings.
explanation: Colour change is mostly used for communication, signalling mood and regulating body temperature.

statement: Hippos sweat blood.
explanation: Hippos secrete a reddish-orange fluid that looks like blood, but it is a mix of pigments that acts as a natural sunscreen and antiseptic.

statement: Dogs see only in black and white.
explanation: Dogs see colour, but with only two types of cone cells they mostly see shades of blue and yellow, not red and green.

statement: Porcupines can shoot their quills at attackers.
explanation: Quills detach very easily on contact, but porcupines cannot throw or shoot them.

statement: All sharks must keep swimming constantly or they will drown.
explanation: Some species such as nurse sharks can pump water over their gills while resting; only certain species rely on constant swimming.

statement: One dog year equals seven human years.
explanation: Dogs age much faster in their first couple of years and then more slowly, and the rate varies with breed and size.

statement: Touching a toad gives you warts.
explanation: Warts are caused by a human virus, not toads, though a toad's skin secretions can irritate the eyes and mouth.

statement: Bats are a type of rodent.
explanation: Bats belong to their own order, Chiroptera, and are more closely related to many hoofed mammals and carnivores than to rodents.

statement: Cats always land safely on their feet.
explanation: Cats have a righting reflex, but falls can still cause serious injuries, especially from low or very high heights.

statement: You swallow eight spiders a year while you sleep.
explanation: This claim is an unsupported myth; spiders avoid sleeping humans and there is no evidence of such a thing happening.

statement: Elephants are afraid of mice.
explanation: There's no evidence for this old myth; elephants are more likely to be startled by sudden, unexpected movement of any kind.

statement: Vampire bats suck blood from their prey.
explanation: Vampire bats make a small cut and lap up the blood with their tongues instead of sucking.

statement: Rabbits are rodents.
explanation: Rabbits and hares belong to the order Lagomorpha, which differs from rodents by having a second pair of upper incisors.

statement: A frog placed in slowly heating water will not jump out until it is boiled.
explanation: Frogs will try to escape as soon as the water gets uncomfortably hot; the 'boiling frog' tale is just a metaphor.

statement: Humans are the only animals that use tools.
explanation: Chimpanzees, crows, otters, octopuses and many other animals use tools to solve problems.

statement: The great white shark is the largest shark.
explanation: The whale shark is the biggest, at up to 12 metres or more, and it feeds on plankton rather than large prey.

statement: Lions are called the king of the jungle because they live in jungles.
explanation: Lions live on grasslands and savannas, not in jungles or rainforests.

statement: All bees die after they sting.
explanation: Only honey bees have a barbed stinger that remains in the skin; bumblebees and many others can sting repeatedly.

statement: Snakes have slimy skin.
explanation: Snake skin is dry and covered in smooth scales.

statement: A purring cat is always a happy cat.
explanation: Cats also purr when they are stressed, in pain or injured, partly as a self-soothing behaviour.

statement: Dogs cool down by sweating all over their bodies like humans.
explanation: Dogs mainly cool down by panting, with a little sweating through the pads of their paws.

statement: Penguins live at the North Pole.
explanation: Penguins live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere; polar bears, not penguins, live in the Arctic.

statement: The African elephant is the largest animal on Earth.
explanation: It is the largest land animal, but the blue whale is far larger and the biggest animal of all time.

statement: Giraffes have more neck vertebrae than other mammals.
explanation: Giraffes have just seven, the same as nearly all other mammals, including mice.

statement: Fish cannot feel pain.
explanation: Fish have nociceptors and show stress behaviours when injured, and many scientists conclude they can experience pain.

statement: Tarantula bites are deadly to humans.
explanation: Tarantula venom is generally no worse than a bee sting, though their urticating hairs can irritate skin and eyes.

statement: Adult clothes moths are the ones that eat holes in your clothes.
explanation: It is the larvae that eat natural fibres such as wool; the adults don't feed at all.

statement: A dog's mouth is cleaner than a human's.
explanation: Dog mouths host many bacteria of their own, and there's no evidence that they are cleaner than human mouths.

statement: Wolves howl at the moon.
explanation: Wolves howl to communicate with their pack, and the moon has nothing to do with it; howling at night just carries well.

statement: Elephants drink by sucking water through their trunk directly into their stomach.
explanation: An elephant sucks water into its trunk and then squirts it into its mouth; the trunk doesn't connect to the stomach.

statement: Goats will eat tin cans.
explanation: Goats are curious and chew on many things, but they can't digest metal and prefer plants, so this is a myth.
